title: Pancreas anatomy: ducts, acini and islets
description: A dual gland: digestive enzymes from acini, hormones from the islets of Langerhans.

questions.question: What does the pancreas do?
questions.answer: Its exocrine tissue releases digestive enzymes into the small intestine. Endocrine islets release hormones such as insulin and glucagon into the blood.

questions.question: Where is the pancreas located?
questions.answer: It lies behind the stomach across the upper abdomen. Its head sits near the duodenum, while its tail reaches toward the spleen.

questions.question: Where is the head of the pancreas?
questions.answer: The broad end nestled in the C-loop of the duodenum, with the uncinate process hooking behind the superior mesenteric vessels. Function: Houses much of the exocrine tissue and the terminal duct.

questions.question: Where is the main pancreatic duct located?
questions.answer: Runs the length of the gland from tail to head, joining the common bile duct at the ampulla in the second part of duodenum. Function: Delivers ~1.5 L of enzyme- and bicarbonate-rich juice daily.

questions.question: What is the function of the acinar cells & ductules?
questions.answer: Function: Secrete the pro-enzymes for digesting protein, fat and carbohydrate. Grape-like clusters of enzyme-packed cells draining into centroacinar cells and ductules.
